rows.object: Thrown item in flight (bottle, can, scrap)
rows.source: thrown.gd:8 (SIZE 15.0 px box, 'a bit big: it has to read in flight'), thrown.gd:38
rows.note: FACT. s = 15/40 = 0.375: a bottle is 25 units * 0.375 = 9.4 px tall in the air vs 4.4 px when it lands (2.14x), i.e. 0.59 m at grid scale, a third of a person's height. Stated as deliberate for readability.

observations: FACT: A person's total height is close to the grid. They are 29.0 px to the top of the hair (skull 28.2), in every build and every view (front 29.0, side 28.8, back 28.5). That is 17.6 px/m for a 1.65 m Thai adult, and 1.81 m at the 16 px/m grid, so only about 10% over. Zombies are 26.7-31.3 px (height 0.92-1.08, zombie.gd:579), which is 1.67-1.96 m. So the person is NOT the vertical outlier. Doors, shutters and storeys are. A door panel is 15*2.0 = 30 px (14.6 px/m for a 2.05 m door). A person reaches 97% of a door's height (real about 80%). The shutter opening is 13.5*2.0 = 27 px (door_prop.gd:126 with world.gd:161), so a person is 2 px TALLER than a shop's shutter opening (confirms h01; real person/opening is about 0.55). A person is also 97% of a 30-px ground storey (real about 0.45). Scaling the person exactly to 16 px/m would change them by only 2.6 px (to 26.4 px).

FACT: The body is super-deformed. Crown to chin is 8.4 px, which is 0.30 of the height (1 : 3.4 heads). A real adult is 1 : 7.5 (0.133). The head is drawn at about 38 px/m tall and 52 px/m wide, the whole body at 17.6 px/m and the legs at 11.7 px/m. Crotch height is 0.31 H (real 0.47), hip joint 0.345 H (real 0.52), knee 0.20 H (real 0.285), shoulder joint 0.64 H (real 0.82). There is no neck: the chin at -19.8 sits on the collar at -20. OPINION: This matters more than any single object size. People judge scale from heads. An 8.4-px head reads as a 0.22 m head, which implies about 38 px/m, so the 30-px doors and storeys around it read as about 0.8 m tall: a doll's house. Part of this is on purpose, for readability (at zoom 4 the eye dots are 2.4 screen px, and hats and hit zones need a big head). But 1:3.4 is chibi. A 1:5-5.5 head (radius about 3.0-3.2 instead of 4.2) with longer legs (HIP_Y about -13.5 instead of -10), keeping the total at about 29 px, would still read and would look adult.

FACT: People are drawn 1.6x too wide. Shoulders including the arms span 11.6 px for build 1.0 (27.6 px/m, against 17.6 px/m for height), which is 0.73 m at the grid. Idle hands are 13.6 px apart. In a 1-cell (16 px) doorway the drawn body fills 73-85% of the width (real about 50-55%). Build (0.9/1.0/1.12) changes only width: 10.8/11.6/12.56 px (rig.gd:55). It never changes height, and survivors have no height variation at all, unlike zombies. The pelvis (6.6 px, look.gd:166) and legs (6.8 px, rig.gd:454) never widen with build or girth. So the fat zombie (girth 1.5) is a 15.6-px torso, 19.2 px across the hands (1.2 m at the grid), on 6.8-px legs, with the same 5-px collision radius.

FACT: The same item is drawn at three unrelated sizes. In the hand it is at body scale (shotgun 18 px, bat 13.5 px = 16-18 px/m). On the ground every pickup is squeezed into one fixed 7x7-px box (main.gd:1496; Items.draw_icon scale = 7/(len+6)*0.95). That makes the shotgun 5.7 px (1/3 of its in-hand size, 5.7 px/m), the bat 5.1, the knife 4.5 and the pistol 3.3 px. A 20 L jerrycan is 3.15x4.4 px (~9 px/m) while a soda can is 1.75x3.5 px (~28 px/m): a jerrycan barely taller than a can (real ratio ~3.9x). In flight (thrown.gd:8, 15-px box) a bottle is 2.14x its size on the ground (9.4 vs 4.4 px). The comment 'at their real size' (main.gd:1491) doesn't match the code. OPINION: This is the cheapest mismatch to fix. It is draw-only and needs no GEN bump: size the ground icon from the weapon's own draw len, or from a per-item real size.

FACT: Held tools are drawn at two scales. Short tools are at the hand's scale: knife 26.6 px/m, razor 29.5, hammer 30, pistol 28, screwdriver 36, scissors 42 (the fist is 4.2 px = 47 px/m). Long weapons are at body-height scale: plank 13, pipe 14, bat 16.1, axe 17.3, shotgun 18 px/m. The axe head (4.2 px out, 5-px edge = 25-45 px/m) is about 2x too big on a true-length haft. OPINION: This split is reasonable and should stay. A 0.32 m knife at 17.6 px/m would be 5.6 px, mostly hidden by the fist. The plank (13 px for about 1 m of ไม้หน้าสาม) is the one long weapon that reads short.

FACT: A seated motorbike rider is taller than when standing. The Wave seat anchor at y -15.5 (bike_art.gd:40) lifts the upper body 5.5 px (rig.gd:337-339), so the head top is at about 34 px against 29 standing (17% taller). A real rider seated on a scooter has about the same head height as standing (about 1.58 vs 1.65 m). Leg reach THIGH+SHIN = 10.4 px is less than the 15.5-px hip height, so a rider can never put a foot on the ground, and the pegs sit at 9.5 px (0.59 m; a real floorboard is about 0.3 m). Cause: the short legs (0.345 H).

FACT: Lying and crouching sizes don't agree. A TopRig sleeper is 31.6 px long (soles +0.5 to hair -31.1, top_rig.gd:20-31), which is 1.98 m on the 1:1 ground. It fills 99% of a 2-cell (32 px) bed (a real 1.65 m sleeper fills about 83% of a 2 m bed), and it is 16.4 px wide (33 px/m). A corpse lying east-west (the side view toppled over) is about 29 px, so the same body is 9% longer lying north-south. observations: FACT: at least four vertical scales exist at once. The person is 17.6 px/m (29 px for 1.65 m; the ground is 16 px/m, which makes him 1.81 m). Doors are 14.6 px/m, the spirit house 15.8, ground windows 13.5, lift doors 11.4, awnings, sala and bus shelter ~10, shophouse storeys 8.0, big buildings 4.7-8.0, BTS, skywalk, poles, lamps, trees and the monument 4.1-6.4, the condo 3.6, compound walls 0. FACT: openings lower than a standing person (29 px): shutter opening 27 (door_prop.gd:126 x2.0; the head overlaps the box -31..-27, confirming h01), lift door 24, temple door 22, side door 28, minimart glass door 28, big-building canopy underside 28, sala eaves 28, BTS station roof 26 above the platform, awning lower edge 25-26, bus shelter roof 23, stair hatch 21. The front door (30) leaves 1 px. Real ratios are: door 1.24x a person, shutter opening 1.8x, ground floor 2.3x.

FACT: the shophouse's shape is inverted. The 6-cell front is 96 px wide and 82 px tall (3F), so it is wider than tall; the real one is 4.1 x 10.8 m, 2.6x taller than wide. Horizontally it is ~23 px/m, because the 1-cell walls (real 0.2 m) are counted in the plot; vertically it is 7.6 px/m. The ground floor is 30 px = 0.97 of a person (real 2.3) and an upper floor 24 px = 0.83 (real 1.8). Someone upstairs pokes 5 px above the next floor line (30 + 29 = 59 vs 54).

FACT: buildings disagree with each other. A condo storey is 11 px while shophouse, flat, office, hospital and mall storeys are all 24 px. A 14F condo (162 px) is only 2x a 3F shophouse (real ~4x). The mall (84) is as tall as a 3F shophouse (82); the real mall is ~1.7x. Office and hospital floors use 24 px like flats although real ones are 25-40% taller. Every big building reuses the shophouse's 30 px ground floor.

FACT: the tall street structures are drawn at about a third of the person's scale. Pole 47 px (1.6 persons; real ~6.4). Lamp head 40. Wires attach at 44 and their lowest mid-span cable hangs at ~30 px, level with a person's crown (overhead.gd:150-154; real >= 5 m). BTS deck 64 px (2.2 persons; real ~6.7) and lower than a 3F shophouse roof (82). Skywalk underside 32 px. Trees 49-59 px (2 persons; real 7+). Monument 286 px = 17.9 m vs real 50 m, its statues 61% of a person. Across families, the bus (30 x 1.6 = 48 px) is taller than the poles and wires and the skywalk, and 75% of the BTS deck (real ~30%).

FACT: compound walls (World.WALL, used around both hospital blocks in the Victory zone and around temples) have no drawn height: a flat tile with 3/4 px strips (world.gd:1132-1134). Yet they block movement and line of sight (world.gd:606, 955). A real 2-2.5 m wall would be 35-44 px at person scale. Gates are bare 5-cell gaps.

FACT: roofs are walkable (world.gd:903-905), but what is on them is toy-sized next to a 29 px person: parapet 3-4 px (real ~1 m = 16-18 px), big-roof stair houses 9 px tall with 8 x 9 px doors, shop water tanks 7 px, compressors 5 px.

FACT (the trade-off): a soi is 3 cells = 48 px, so every shophouse (h 58/82) already lifts its roof over the whole soi behind it and 10-34 px of the opposite ground floor. At a consistent 16-17.6 px/m a 3F shophouse would be ~173-190 px and cover 11-12 cells, which includes the opposite row's shop fronts. Two fades already exist: main.gd:1308-1317 turns a building in front of the local player to 30% alpha, and main.gd:1319-1339 fades the BTS and skywalk when you are under them. Heights (GROUND_H, FLOOR_H, stretches, BTS_H, pole, tree, parapet) are draw-side only. storey_lift also places people upstairs and throws (player.gd:860, combat.gd:151-153), but none of it needs a CityGen.GEN bump. Wall thickness, stair length, soi width and plot size do need one.

OPINION: the smallest change that fixes the most is to make the openings clear the person before making towers tall. For example: ground floor ~48-54 px, door ~36, shutter opening ~44-48 with the box and sign above it, upper floors ~36-40, parapet ~12-16, compound wall ~32-36 px drawn as a real standing wall. Then derive street structures from one declared factor rather than separate constants: pole/lamp ~110-150, BTS ~130-160, trees 90-150 with a trunk a person can walk under. Put condo floors on FLOOR_H. Pair taller buildings with a broader version of the existing fade (every building whose visual_rect covers the player or a nearby zombie, not just one), because squat roofs are what currently hide the soi problem.

observations: FACT: The character is drawn at two different scales. It is 29 px tall (17.6 px/m for a 1.65 m adult), but the hip is at 10 px (11.6 px/m) and the head is 8.4 px across (about 38 px/m). The figure is about 3.5 heads tall, where a real adult is about 7.5 (rig.gd:216-222, look.gd:32,626-646). The body below the neck works out to about 11.6-14.5 px/m; the oversized head adds the rest. So whether a piece of furniture looks right depends on which part of the person you compare it to.

FACT: Waist-level things were sized to the legs, not to the whole person. Table 8 px (10.7 px/m), counter 11 (11.6), sink 11 (12.9), glass counter 12.5 (12.5), stove top 9.5 (11.9), food cart 18 (11.6), stool 5 (SEAT_HEIGHT chairs 5 = half the hip). They meet the hip correctly, but next to the whole figure they are 30-40% too low: counter 0.38 of the person's height vs 0.58 real, table 0.28 vs 0.45, stool 0.17 vs 0.27.

FACT: Every tall piece is at or below the person's height, and each has its own stretch value (TALL in furniture_prop.gd:10): fridge 28.35 px (17.7 px/m), shelf 28 (15.6), pantry 22.4 (14.0), wardrobe 26 (13.7), vending 24 (13.0), lift doors 24 (11.4), stairs 17. So a 1.9 m wardrobe (26 px), a 1.85 m vending machine (24) and a 2.1 m lift door (24) are all shorter than a 1.65 m person (29), where real life has them 12-27% taller. A 1.6 m fridge is drawn taller than the 1.9 m wardrobe. Interior doors (30 px) are only 1 px taller than a person. TALL also stretches the details (the wardrobe's drawer fronts become 10 px tall).

FACT: Seat heights follow two different references. The stool follows the legs (5 px = 0.5 of the hip, real 0.52). The sofa (8), bench (7.5), barber chair (9), exam couch (9) and recliner (8) follow the whole person instead: their seats are 0.75-0.9 of the hip vs about 0.5-0.64 real, so a seated character's knees barely bend (player.gd:931).

FACT: Widths are locked to one cell. Almost everything is 12-16 px wide (usually 14) whatever its real width, so width scales range from 7.8 to 36 px/m. Too small: sofa (a 1.8 m sofa in 16 px, 8.9 px/m), exam couch (1 m long, a lying body is 30-34 px), food cart 10, waiting bench 9.4, altar 10.8, bed width 14 px (reads as a single bed, 9.3 px/m against a 1.5 m family bed), and the single-cell bed is 16 px long (half a person). Too big: fridge 23.3, safe 20, tool cabinet 20, tap basin 24, radio 36.

FACT: Ground depth is drawn with at least five different amounts of squash. The bed down the room is 1:1 with the grid (about 28 px for about 1.8 m). The same bed across the room is only 10 px deep, the floor mattress 7 px for 0.9 m (about 0.5), the toilet pan 0.6, tyres 0.45, and shadows and bikes 0.35 (bike_art.gd:69, furniture_prop.gd:48). Every standing piece (fridge, shelf, table, counter, sofa, vending) is a flat billboard with a 1.5 px lit top. A table shows 2 px of top where a 0.8 m top would be 12.8 px at grid scale or 4.5 px at 0.35.

FACT: Walls take half the building. Every wall (party, outer, inner) is a whole 1 m cell, drawn flat with no height when the roof is lifted (world.gd:1127-1130), while the doors in them stand 30 px tall. In the 6x13 shophouse plans, 40 of 78 cells (51%) are walls or openings, against about 10% for real 0.1-0.2 m walls. Room sizes (shop 4x6-8, bathroom 1x2, bedroom 4x3) only come out real because the plots are 6-7 m apart (city_gen.gd:70) instead of about 4-4.5 m.

FACT: Clear one-off mistakes: (1) The repair shop's motorbike is 14.5 px long with 5 px wheels, half the size of the parked and ridden bikes (30 px, 9 px wheels, bike_art.gd:373), and it is placed on the pavement right next to them (city_gen.gd:1172). Its tyre stack has 12 px tyres, bigger than either bike's wheels. (2) The stairs fit in 1 cell with 5 steps reaching 17 px, but the floor above is 30 px up; a real flight needs about 4 m and about 20 steps. (3) The bulb hangs at y -23, level with the character's face. (4) The radio (10x6 px on the floor) is about 2.2x too big. (5) The plant-room generator (16x11 px in 1 cell) is 2x a portable set but only about a third of a real building generator. (6) The feather flag (30 px) is only as tall as a person; real ones are about 3 m.

FACT: These already agree with the person's height within about 10%: jar (0.45 vs 0.48), sofa (0.52 vs 0.52 back height), waiting bench, barber chair (0.72 vs 0.70), recliner (0.62 vs 0.64), hair-wash basin (0.59 vs 0.64), wheelchair (0.55 vs 0.56), Buddha shelf (1.14 vs 1.21), fridge as a 1.6 m home fridge (0.98 vs 0.97), bed length (about 15.5 px/m), and the 1x2 m bathroom.

OPINION: A fix that only changes drawing (footprints stay the same, so no CityGen.GEN bump): pick one height rule tied to the character, and redraw each piece at that height instead of stretching it with TALL. Rule: real height up to 0.9 m at 11.6 px/m (keeps seats, tables and the rig poses working); 0.9 m to 1.65 m rising from 10 px to 29 px; above that, +17.6 px per metre. Results: table 8.7, counter 12, stand fan 19, fridge 28, shelf 31.6, wardrobe 33, vending 32.5, drinks cooler and doors 35, lift doors 37. Also draw widths inside the cell by real width (fridge and safe about 10 px, tap about 8, radio about 5), and scale the decor bike and tyres to match bike_art. Pieces longer than 1 m (sofa, family bed, exam couch, food cart, bench, counter run) would need 2-cell footprints, which means a GEN bump; alternatively they can overhang the next cell without blocking it, as the floor mattress and stools already do. Trade-off: 33-37 px pieces cover about 2 cells of floor behind them when the roof is lifted (for example, a fridge in row 'Wf..FW' would hide the kitchen row behind it). One option is to fade a tall piece while someone stands behind it, in the same way people fade; this is not a dark shade over the area, which the user rejected. The 'stripped' and 'highlight' overlay heights (furniture_prop.gd:201,206, 18 and 23 x TALL) would need to follow.

observations: FACT: bikes and four-wheelers use two different length scales. All 13 bike models are drawn close to true length at 16.2-18.5 px/m (Wave 32.1 px = 1.93 m). Every VEHICLE_SCALE vehicle is 53-77% of real length: tuk-tuk 8.5 px/m, army 9.8, pickup and songthaew 10.0, van 10.1, taxi 10.8, sedan 11.0, bus 12.3. So a sedan is 1.55 Waves long (real 2.33), and a tuk-tuk (25.6 px) is shorter than every motorbike (32.1-39.1 px), though it is really about 1.55 bikes long.

FACT: VEHICLE_SCALE is one uniform factor (world.gd:242 sets scale to Vector2.ONE*1.6), but the art's length:height ratios are off by different amounts for each kind: sedan 1.82 (real 3.1), van 1.79 (2.35), pickup 2.2 (2.94), songthaew 1.83 (2.3), bus 3.08 (3.75), tuk-tuk 0.8 (1.71), army 3.83 (2.5, too flat). OPINION: changing the factor cannot fix them. Raising it to 2.32 gives the sedan its 4.5 m (72 px) but also a 39 px (2.5 m) roof. Each kind needs its own length and height, i.e. the BODY table and _car_side/_car_end/_tuktuk/_army redrawn to real L and H at 16 px/m ground.

FACT: heights compared with the person (29 px; 17.6 px/m if 1.65 m). Sedan roof 27.2 (+7%, fine), taxi 30.4 with sign, tuk-tuk 32 (fine), bus 48 (-14%, about 56 needed), van 30.4 (-24%, about 40), pickup cab 24 (-25%, about 32: drawn lower than a person although a Hilux cab is taller than a Thai adult), songthaew canopy 28.8 (-30%, about 40), army truck 19.2 (-64%, about 53). The whole army truck sits at shoulder height (shoulders at -18.6 px).

FACT: bikes are true length but too tall above the wheels. Wheels are correct (7.6-12.4 px), but mirrors and screens reach 22-31 px (1.4-1.9 m at 16 px/m against 1.0-1.44 m real) and seats sit at 15.5-19 px (0.97-1.19 m against 0.75-0.89 m), 19-25 px/m vertically. The Forza screen (31 px) is taller than the van roof (30.4) and the sedan roof (27.2). The seated rider's head top is 34.5 px (Wave) to 38 px (trail), 19-31% taller than the same person standing, and above every car, van, pickup and songthaew roof. Cause (fact): the rig's hips are at HIP_Y -10 with 10.4 px legs (36% of height against about 47% real), and the seats are raised so the feet reach pegs at -9 to -11.5 px.

FACT: depth (north-south) follows three different rules. (a) Ground and buildings are 1:1, 16 px per metre north-south. (b) Characters and bikes are foreshortened (FOOT_DEPTH 0.4, BikeArt.DEPTH 0.35: a bike parked N-S spans 7.35 px between its wheels). (c) Four-wheelers side-on are 1-cell billboards (1 m deep against 1.75-2.5 m, shadow 9.6 px, no roof plane). End-on they are 25.6 px wide for everything from a sedan to the bus (the bus is 64% of its real width), with an 8 px front face (bus 24 px) and a roof seen from above. End-on span is sedan 48 px and bus 125 px, against about 95 px and 245 px under the buildings' rule (footprint 1:1 + facade h). The same car is 1.0 m wide side-on and 1.6 m wide end-on.

FACT: footprints (VEHICLE_CELLS + _size_vehicles) are sedan/taxi/van/pickup/songthaew 3 cells (3 m against 4.5-5.4 m), bus 9 (12 m), army 5 (7.5 m), tuk-tuk 2 (3 m). True lengths would be about 5, 5-6, 12, 8 and 3 cells. FACT: _size_vehicles is a post-pass that draws no random numbers, and it skips cells that are not free (city_gen.gd:1262-1265). OPINION: longer blocked footprints could probably be added there without re-rolling the city (maybe no GEN bump), but check first: _landmarks (the minivan stand, via _fits) and later passes read w.blocked.

FACT, collision mismatches: a vertical bus blocks 144 px but is drawn 125 px, leaving about 19 px of invisible wall at its north end. A side-on van is drawn to 55.2 px over 48 px of blocked cells (7 px overhang into a free cell), a pickup 5.6 px. On a flipped wreck the stand-on height is 15.6 px (roof_spot *0.65) while its drawn top is 25.3 px, so a figure's feet end up about 10 px inside the body.

FACT: big-vehicle wheels are too small. Bus wheel 10.2 px and army 9.6 px, about the same as the sedan (9.0) and the Wave (9.0). Real bus and truck wheels are 1.0-1.1 m (16-18 px). The trail bike's front wheel (12.4 px) is bigger than the bus's.

FACT: lane markings always divide a road into quarters (lines at wd/4, the centre, 3wd/4; world.gd:1190-1194, 1207-1211). The 14-wide avenues with a median come out at 3.5 m + 2.75 m per carriageway (real widths, half the lane count), but 10-wide roads get 2.5 m lanes, 8-wide (Soi Rang Nam, Yothi) 2.0 m, and 6-wide (the Rang Nam spur, ROAD_W towns) 1.5 m, which is narrower than an end-on car (25.6 px). Sois are 3 m (real 4-6 m) and pavements 2 m, so a side-on parked bike (32-39 px) covers the whole pavement width. OPINION: pick the lane count from the width (about 3-3.5 m per lane), e.g. 8 cells = 2 lanes plus parking, 6 cells = 2 lanes. This is a draw-only change.

FACT, compared with other families: van roof 30.4 px equals the shophouse GROUND_H of 30 px (a 2.3 m van as tall as a 3.5-4 m shop storey). The bus is 48 px, 1.6 shop ground floors, and reaches 75% of the BTS deck lift BTS_H 64 px (real about 3.2 m under about 10-12 m). The bus-stop roof underside (23 px) is below a standing person's head (29 px), next to a bus door 35 px tall.

FACT, art details: wrecks are rotated 0.2-0.5 rad in the screen plane (street_prop.gd:447), so side-on wrecks float a wheel 3.4-8.7 px off the ground and dip the other end up to about 5.8 px below it; they read as tipped, not slewed across the lane. Tuk-tuks are forced side-on (city_gen.gd:986), so on N-S roads they are drawn crosswise to traffic. The minivan stand's destination card (street_prop.gd:329) floats above the roof (y -24..-20, roof -19). Songthaew and tuk-tuk headroom (6.4 px and 8 px) is less than half a seated torso (19 px). The long-tail boat is unscaled at 46 px (2.9 m against 6+ m).

OPINION, target sizes on one scale (ground 16 px/m, heights tied to the person at 29 px = 1.65 m, about 17.6 px/m): sedan 72 px long, roof about 25.5; taxi the same plus the sign; van 86 x about 40; pickup 85 x about 32; songthaew 85 x about 40; bus 192 x about 56; tuk-tuk 48 x about 31; army truck 120 x about 53; end-on widths 28 px (car) to 40 px (bus). Occlusion cost: only the van, pickup and songthaew (+8-12 px) and the army truck (+34 px) grow taller, each hiding at most 1-2 more cells of road north of it, much less than a 2-3 storey roof. The longer bodies cost road space, not view. Bikes need the opposite: keep their length and lower the bodies about 20% (seat about 13 px); that is tied to the rig's short legs, which is a separate decision.

It runs windowed on port 9536; the last run's log is scale/run5.txt. `git status` is clean afterwards.

HOW THEY WERE MADE (fact)
- The props are new instances of the game's own classes (StreetProp, TreeProp, DoorProp, FurnitureProp, DecorProp). They use the same scale factors World._spawn_props applies (world.gd:161, 242, 506): VEHICLE_SCALE 1.6 (street_prop.gd:10), TreeProp.SCALE 1.4 (tree_prop.gd:6), DOOR_STRETCH 2.0 (door_prop.gd:7).
- I placed them by script. The buildings, the road, the room and the BTS station are the real ones where the game put them.
- The people are stand-ins drawn with Look.draw (front view, the player's own look). The real player is hidden, because the game camera follows the mouse aim (main.gd:1036), so I used a separate Camera2D.
- Existing street props and trees inside each frame were hidden.
- Sizes were measured offscreen: each node drawn at 3x in a SubViewport, then the bounding box of pixels with alpha >= 0.5, so shadows don't count.
- 16 px = 1 m.
- The "จริง" (real-life) sizes in the labels are my own approximate references. They are opinion, not measurements.

SEED (fact, affects the earlier review shots)
`seed(11)` followed by `host()` does not reproduce the same city. main.gd:291 takes `randi()` only after the scene has been instantiated. My exploration run and my first real run got different layouts: flats at (53,27) vs (58,27), and the canal-side row at x 288-395 was different. So cells quoted from earlier screenshots, such as the gold shop near (100,260) or Ratchawithi at (100,160), may not match. I fixed this with `host(9536, false, true, 11)`, which uses city_seed 11 on every run.

WHAT THE IMAGES SHOW (opinion)
There are three vertical scales at once:
- **About 1:1:** people, doors, furniture, jars, motorbikes and the bus. People run about 10% tall, which makes doors and shutters read as small next to them.
- **Shortened:** cars, pickups, vans, songthaews and the tuk-tuk are drawn at 53-70% of real length. Heights are near real, except the army truck (about 40%) and the pickup (about 83%).
- **Squashed:** everything tall. Storeys are about 50%, big buildings 45-50%, poles and trees 25-40%, the BTS about 30%, the bus shelter about 60%.

So a storey is drawn about as tall as a person, and everything tall tops out at about 2-3 people. This matches the roof-hiding trade-off: raising storeys, poles, trees and the BTS toward real heights is where "สมส่วน" (well-proportioned) and "the roof hides the soi" pull against each other. The cheapest mismatches to fix look draw-only: the army truck, the tuk-tuk, the bus shelter roof below head height, a shutter shorter than a person, and the condo formula.

CAVEATS
- The staged props sit where no CityGen layout would put them (for example, a car on the pavement). They are for size comparison only.
- The facade heights are BuildingProp.h, the facade itself; the roof is drawn on top of that.

designs.rule: One metre is 16 px, the size of one tile, in every direction: across, north-south on the ground, and straight up the screen. Take the real object's size in metres and multiply by 16. Draw its front face that tall. If you would see its top from a first-floor window, also draw a top face as deep as the object really is, lifted by its height. That is exactly how buildings already draw their roofs. There are no stretch factors: DOOR_STRETCH, WINDOW_STRETCH, TALL, TreeProp.SCALE and VEHICLE_SCALE all end at 1.0. Only two things may be off. The person is 29 px, which reads as a tall man of about 1.80 m, 6-10% over. Small hand tools stay at hand scale so they can be read.

designs.occlusion_plan:
FACT: in this projection anything of height H hides H px of ground north of its back wall (roof = Rect2(0,-h-d,w,d), building_prop.gd:164). At 16 px/m a 3-storey shophouse (172 px) hides 10.75 cells behind it. That covers a 3-cell soi plus 7.75 cells of the opposite row, i.e. its whole shop front. On an east-west road (14 + 2x2 cells between rows), the row south of the road hides the pavement and about 9 of the 14 road cells. A 7-storey block (376 px) hides 23.5 cells. No realistic soi width fixes this (5 cells = 80 px), so a peel is mandatory, not optional.

PROPOSAL, the "street-open peel", replacing today's single-building 0.3 fade (main.gd:1308-1318):
1) Triggers. Run at 10 Hz, client only. Points: the local player's body; every other survivor; every zombie or player with sight_k > 0 (already computed in main.gd:1180-1187, so peeling never reveals anyone out of line of sight); and a few sample points along the soi or road cells the player stands in, inside the screen. A building is peeled when its roof shadow (x in [x0, x0+w], y in [back-h, back], back = position.y - d) contains a trigger point, or when it covers the player (today's rule, including the "inside a building" case at main.gd:1316). Lookup: for each point, walk the cells south of it up to max h/16 (11 for shophouses, 24 for flats) through world.building_at. There is no scan over all buildings. Hysteresis: a building stays peeled 1.5 s after its last trigger, so moving zombies don't make roofs flicker.
2) Look. One shared canvas_item clip shader discards everything above the ground-floor ceiling (local VERTEX.y < -GROUND_H). The MeshCanvas mesh is in the node's local coordinates (mesh_canvas.gd:203), so signs drawn as text are clipped too. A baked child "cap" node draws the rest of the footprint as a flat roof-coloured plate at ground level with a 1 px parapet line. The peeled building then reads as a normal one-storey building whose roof stops at its own back wall. Nothing is drawn north of the back wall, so the soi or road is fully clear. The interior stays covered, so there is no free look into neighbours' shops, and it is not a dark shade (the user rejected those). Animate by sliding the cut line from h down to GROUND_H in 0.16 s, using a per-building material only while animating; at most about 10 at once. The glow child (night windows) is hidden above the cut while peeled. Never peel a building someone visible is standing on (on_roof).
3) Same trigger for other tall things. Tree canopies fade to about 0.35 (extend the loop at main.gd:1302). The BTS deck already fades (main.gd:1320-1339, driven by BTS_H). Tall furniture (1.6 m or more) fades to 0.4 while a character stands in the 2 cells north of it. Poles are thin and need nothing.
4) Accepted, and realistic: an empty soi under an unpeeled roof stays hidden. From the street you cannot see into a 3 m lane between 10 m buildings.
5) Zoom. The viewport is 1280x720 (project.godot:23-24) at play_zoom 4 (main.gd:131), so 180 world px, 11 cells, are visible vertically. A 172 px front would fill 96% of the screen. Proposed: default play_zoom 3 (240 px, about 70%); Ctrl+wheel stays.
6) Fallback if the clip shader misbehaves: the same trigger can drive today's alpha fade (0.3 -> 0.2). It is cheaper, but 172-376 px translucent facades over a street turn into visual mush. Rejected alternative: silhouettes of hidden characters. They cost a second GDScript draw of every hidden character, and characters are the frame cost.
PERF (honest): the peel is static-drawing work, a material swap plus toggling one node. No building is redrawn per frame. Per frame the cost is about (visible characters) x 11-24 dictionary lookups at 10 Hz. Taller visual_rects stream more building nodes around the camera (world.gd:140), about 2x more rows south of the screen. Larger facades and canopies mean more overdraw: negligible on desktop, but measure on web first, per the perf-escalation order. The per-frame cost of character drawing does not change.
designs.tradeoffs:
WHAT YOU GAIN: every object shares one ruler that a beginner can apply (metres x 16). Buildings stop contradicting themselves: roofs are already drawn at 16 px/m depth, but walls are at 8 px/m. Doors, shutters, storeys, cars, trees and the BTS stand in their real ratios to a person: a door is 1.14 people tall, a shutter opening 1.65, a ground floor 2.1, a 3-storey front 5.9, a pole 5.5, the BTS rail 6. That is the "สมส่วนสมจริง" (well-proportioned and realistic) the user describes.
WHAT YOU PAY:
(1) It becomes a street-level diorama. At zoom 4 a 3-storey front fills the screen, tall blocks run off the top of the screen, and you see less map and more street. The user must see a prototype before committing.
(2) The row between the camera and you is always cut down to one storey. Realism holds for the row you face and the rows further north, not the row behind you. It is a deliberate stage-set cut, and roofs will pop between tall and cut as zombies move. Hysteresis and the slide soften this but don't remove it.
(3) The big head (1:3.4) stays unless the optional rig pass is done. Next to real doors and storeys a person will still read a little doll-like.
(4) Widths are locked to one cell. The 1.8 m sofa, 1.5 m bed, 5-cell cars and 12-cell bus need footprints, which means a GEN bump. Until then some things overhang their cells.
(5) The squeezed district (half the lanes, 3 m sois, poles every 6 m, 1 m walls) looks more obviously squeezed next to true heights: a canyon feel.
VERSUS THE CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE: one compressed vertical scale (about 8-10 px/m) for buildings, furniture and vehicles, with the person exempt. It has less occlusion and less work, but it is not true proportions: the person stays the outlier. This proposal deliberately picks truth and pays for it with the peel.

designs.rule: Everything on the ground (lengths, widths, footprints, wheel diameters) is 16 px per metre, and 1 cell = 1 m. Heights all come from one function, World.up(metres), which uses the character as the ruler: floor 0 m = 0 px, hip 0.86 m = 10 px (Rig.HIP_Y), top of head 1.65 m = 29 px, door head 2.0 m = 35 px. Below 2 m, an object reaches the same part of the body that it would in real life. Every metre above 2 m adds only 8 px, so storeys, poles, trees and the BTS keep their true ratios to each other without hiding the street. Round parts (wheels, jars) keep their real ground size, and anything a person walks through or under must be at least up(2.05) = 36 px tall.

designs.occlusion_plan: FACT: At play zoom 4 (main.gd:131, 156) the 1280x720 viewport (project.godot:23-24) shows 320x180 world px = 20x11.25 cells. The camera centres on the chest (main.gd:1040), so about 105 px above the feet and 75 px below are on screen. Every building hides exactly h px of ground north of its back wall (the roof is the footprint lifted by h, building_prop.gd:59, 72). FACT: A soi is 48 px (city_gen.gd:28, 782), so today's 2F (58) and 3F (82) rows ALREADY hide 100% of the soi behind them, plus 10-34 px of the opposite row's shop fronts. Today's readability therefore comes only from the fade (main.gd:1296-1339): alpha 0.3 on a building whose visual_rect overlaps the LOCAL player's 12x28 body; trees within dy 0..3, dx ±2 at 0.45; the BTS/skywalk when you stand under it. Zombies in a soi one building to the side of you stay hidden. Under the curve: 2F 80, 3F 104 (+22 px = +1.4 cells; on an E-W road, the roofs of the buildings to its south, which back onto it, now cover 6.5 cells of its south side instead of 5.1). The BTS deck band is the same size but drawn 48 px (3 cells) further north. Tree crowns reach ~106 px. PLAN (OPINION, draw-only): (1) Cutaway fade. In main._fade_trees_near, besides the body test, fade every BuildingProp, TreeProp and the overhead in world.near(pos, 3) whose visual_rect overlaps the body rect (feet to 30 px up) of ANY character the local player currently sees (the existing sight fade already hides those behind walls, since BUILDING/WALL block sight, world.gd:955), and whose front line is south of that character's feet. Throttle to 10 Hz (~40 buildings x <=60 characters = ~2.4k rect tests). Tween alpha over FADE 0.16 s, with a 0.3 s hold to stop flicker. (2) Tree fade window dy 0..6, dx -3..3. (3) With the roof lifted, tall furniture (>=1.8 m: shelf, cooler, wardrobe, vending, pegboard) fades to 0.45 when a seen character stands behind it. (4) Compound walls stay opaque: they already block sight, so their new 36 px face hides nothing the player could see. (5) No dark shade over unseen areas (the user rejected it); only occluders fade, and people keep their existing sight fade. (6) Heights never exceed the curve. Condos (368 px for 14F) exist only in backdrop zones; if they feel oppressive, cap drawn floors at 10 (272 px). WHY NOT KEEP EVERYTHING SQUAT: the soi is already fully covered at today's heights, so the fade rule is what makes the ground readable whatever the scale. The curve only adds 1.4 cells.
designs.tradeoffs: FACT (rejected alternatives, with numbers): (a) One true scale for everything (17.6 px/m): the ground floor would be 63, upper floors 53, and a 3F shophouse 187 px, taller than the whole 180 px view. Poles would be 158 and the BTS 204. (b) One compressed scale for everything including people, at today's storey scale of 8 px/m: the person would be 13.2 px, the head 3.8 px with 0.27 px eyes, and limb outlines 1.6 px. The ~220 hard-coded y values in look/clothes/rig would collapse. Keeping the character's screen size would need zoom 8.8, which shows 145x82 px = 9x5 cells, a quarter of today's view: fatal for a horde game. (c) A middle uniform scale of 11 px/m: the person would be 18 px AND the 3F shophouse 117 px, so smaller people and more occlusion than the curve (104). So the person must stay the 29 px ruler, and the compression goes above the door head. COSTS OF THE CURVE (FACT): ratios above 2 m are 0.45x of real. A person is 0.60 of the ground floor (real 0.46), a bus 1.55 persons (real 1.94), a 3F shophouse 3.6 persons (real 6.4). Real-taller always stays game-taller (the curve is monotonic), so nothing is ever out of order: bus 45 < ground floor 48 < wires 71 < pole 91 < 3F roof 104 < BTS 112. The ground floor to upper floor ratio becomes 2:1 (real 1.2-1.5:1). OPINION: it reads like an old shophouse with a tall shop floor. If it looks off, raise the architecture slope to 9.3 px/m (FLOOR_H 28, 3F 115). The facade stays 96 wide x 104 tall (1.08:1; real 2.6:1) because plots are 6-7 cells for 4-4.5 m real (only a GEN change fixes that). Below the hip, heights run at 11.6 px/m because of the chibi legs (HIP_Y -10 = 0.345 H). Seats, tables and counters therefore meet the rig correctly, but round wheels at ground scale sit 2-3 px above the curve, so bikes are built up from their wheels (seat 11, not 8.8). The BTS deck now visually covers the north pavement and shop fronts of Phahon Yothin instead of the north lanes. Trees cover ~2.5x today's area. The scene will look ghosted (faded) more often.
designs.risks: (1) Literal px tied to the old GROUND_H 30 are spread around (bulb decor_prop.gd:93, stairs :86-91, lift doors :293-300, sala building_prop.gd:50, market stalls :763-765, temple door 22, BTS stairs -46, station roof -26). Any one missed leaves a door or light at the wrong height; re-run the lineup script (scratchpad scale_lineups.gd, port 9536) after each stage. (2) Stretch-based doors, shutters and windows distort line widths (shutter ribs 3.3 px, window boards 7 px). A native redraw is cleaner. (3) storey_lift(1) 30 -> 48 moves the upper floor plan 3 cells up. Camera (main.gd:1040), throws (combat.gd:151-153), roof lifts (world.gd:903-905, player.gd:860) and prompts (main.gd:1263) follow automatically, but stairs transitions and decals_up need a play test. Standing on a 3F roof lifts 104 px (the camera zooms out to 0.78x on roofs). (4) The cutaway can flicker, or fade half the street in a horde: it needs hysteresis/tween and a cap (e.g., at most 6 buildings faded). The per-frame rect tests are GDScript work, so throttle to 10 Hz (moving characters are already the perf cost). (5) Vehicles: roof_spot/roof_area/middle/draw_shift all multiply by VEHICLE_SCALE. Redrawing in metres means rewriting them together, or climbing onto roofs breaks. Doing heights before lengths (before the GEN stage) leaves a stubby army truck (73.6 x 43) for a while. (6) Longer vehicle footprints change w.blocked. _size_vehicles uses no RNG, but saved zombies and pickups could land inside newly blocked cells, so bundle them into the GEN bump. (7) Compound walls as y-sorted props are new code (sorting against characters on both sides, gates). (8) The wire lift is baked at generation (city_gen.gd:908). This is safe because cities are rebuilt from the seed, but moving it into overhead.gd avoids confusion. (9) Taste: the user may find taller trees and the higher BTS hide too much. Tune the two numbers (architecture slope 8 px/m, tree scale) rather than the rule. (10) Character reproportioning (smaller head, longer legs) is NOT part of this. If it is done later, move the hip anchor in World.up() (e.g., 12.5 px) and the lower band becomes almost linear.

designs.rule: Across the ground, 1 m = 16 px (one cell), as it is now. Going up the screen, anything up to 3 m high also uses 16 px per metre, and the person (29 px) counts as 1.8 m. So a door is 34 px, a shutter opening 45, a car roof 23 and a bus roof 51. Things below the hip (seats, beds, tables, counters, stoves, jars) keep matching the person's body instead (knee about 5 px, hand about 11 px), because the legs are short. Above 3 m, each extra metre is only 8 px (px = 48 + 8 × (metres − 3)): an upper storey is 24 px, a 10 m pole 104, an 11 m BTS deck 112. Heights start again from whatever floor someone stands on (an upstairs room, a roof, a vehicle roof).

designs.occlusion_plan: FACT: a roof covers h px of ground north of its building's back wall. Sois are 3 cells (48 px), so they are already fully covered at today's 58/82 px. PLAN: raise heights only where the eye compares them with a person. Above 3 m the scale is halved, so upper storeys stay 24 px. Every shophouse grows by 22 px: 18 px of taller ground floor and 4 px of parapet (2F 58 -> 80, 3F 82 -> 104). That is 1.4 more cells of roof, and it lands on the back rooms of the next row north, which sit under their own roof anyway. The new tall street things are mostly thin: poles, lamps and BTS pillars hide almost nothing. In Victory the station code treats the skytrain line as running north-south (overhead.gd:101, a fixed x), so raising the deck mostly slides it along itself (opinion; check the east-west parts of bts_path). All of the fixes below extend the existing see-through fade in main.gd._fade_trees_near (1296-1339). None of them is a dark shade, and none needs a GEN bump. (1) Buildings: at main.gd:1308, test visual_rect against a 'look box' around the player, about Rect2(pos + (-48,-64), (96,68)), 6 cells wide, instead of the 12x28 body box. Then neighbouring roofs that cover the soi next to you fade to 0.3 too, not only the one over your body. (2) Trees: dy 0..3 -> 0..6 and dx -2..2 -> -3..3 for the taller canopies. (3) Inside a building, also fade its front DoorProps and shutters. At 34-45 px they would hide the front 2-3 rows of the shop floor, and doors are never faded today. (4) Optional: run the same tree and building test for each zombie the local player can currently see (a few dictionary lookups each), so a zombie near you is never hidden under a canopy or roof. Wide furniture stays one cell, and tall furniture grows by only 3-6 px, so indoor occlusion hardly changes.
designs.tradeoffs: (1) The upper storeys look half as tall as the ground floor (24 vs 48 px; in real life the ratio is about 1:1.2). It reads as a tall shop with a fascia (shutter box and sign band) and two squat floors over it. It is still far more believable than today's person-height storeys, and the 96-px front becomes taller than wide (104 px), closer to the real tall, narrow shophouse. (2) The person stays chibi (head 1:3.4, 10-px legs), which is the largest 'toy' cue left. Low furniture and bike seats deliberately keep matching those short legs, so the rule has a 'below the hip, match the body' clause. (3) Vehicles get 1.4-1.9x longer (the tuk-tuk and army truck most), so roads look fuller, more road cells are blocked, and a few parked cars overlap their neighbours' drawings. End-on vehicles keep today's 1.6 m width (the bus looks too narrow end-on) to avoid touching draw_shift and the collision overhang boxes. (4) Trees, poles, lamps and the BTS roughly double in height, so more of the screen is overhead clutter, and the canopies need the wider fade. The lamp light pool stays at 4 m. (5) The monument (286 px), mall and office storey heights, the 1-cell stair (5 steps to a 48-px ceiling), wall thickness and plot sizes are left alone. Fixing them needs either more occlusion or a GEN bump. (6) The person counts as 1.8 m, about 10% tall for a Thai adult. Shrinking them 2.6 px would touch every character file, which isn't worth it.

judge.summary: I checked the code. The ground is 16 px per metre (1 cell = 1 m) and a person is 29 px, which reads as a 1.8 m adult. Every other family gets its height from its own separate setting: GROUND_H 30 and FLOOR_H 24 (building_prop.gd:7-8), DOOR_STRETCH 2.0 shared by doors and shutters (door_prop.gd:7, world.gd:161), TALL for furniture (furniture_prop.gd:10), one VEHICLE_SCALE of 1.6 for every vehicle (street_prop.gd:10, world.gd:242), TreeProp.SCALE 1.4, BTS_H 64 and a pole 47 px tall. The results: a ground floor (30 px) is as tall as a person, the shutter opening (27 px) is 2 px lower than a head, cars are 53-77% of their real length, and poles, trees and the BTS stop at about two people tall. The root cause is the trade-off in the brief. A roof hides h px of ground behind it, and a 48-px soi is already fully hidden by today's 58-82 px shophouses, so buildings were kept squat and each family was patched with its own stretch. Full true scale (proposal A) would make a 3-storey front 172 px tall while zoom 4 shows only 180 px, and it would need a roof-cutting system, so I reject it. I recommend proposal C's two-slope rule with B's see-through rule: true size (16 px/m) up to 3 m, the zone where the eye compares things with a person, and only 8 px for each metre above that. Storeys, poles, trees and the BTS then keep their real order and ratios to each other, and a 3-storey shophouse grows only from 82 to 104 px (+1.4 cells of roof). The street stays readable because today's see-through fade is extended from the local player to every character you can currently see. That also fixes a present bug: a zombie you can see gets hidden under a neighbouring roof. Everything is draw-only (no CityGen.GEN bump). The chibi character (head 1:3.4 of body height, legs 0.35 of it) is the biggest toy-like cue left, and whether to change it is a separate decision for the user.
judge.recommended: Merge: 'Person ruler, true to 3 m, half-scale sky' (proposal C's two-slope rule, vehicle redraw with 1 drawing unit = 10 cm, and no-reset blocking pass) + proposal B's 'see-through for every character you can see' occlusion (10 Hz, hold, tween) + proposal A's native redraws (stretches kept only as a stepping stone) and ground pickups at real size.
judge.rule: ONE RULER, TWO SLOPES. (1) On the ground nothing changes: 1 cell = 1 m = 16 px for every length and width. (2) Up the screen, use 16 px per metre up to 3 m, then 8 px per metre above 3 m: px = 16*m when m <= 3, px = 48 + 8*(m - 3) above. Add a helper World.up(m) so nobody does this sum by hand. (3) The person is the ruler: 29 px, counted as a 1.8 m adult. Nothing a person walks through or under may be lower than 34 px (a 2.1 m door head). (4) Anything below the hip is placed where it meets THIS body, not by metres: hip = 10 px, so a seat is about 5, a table 8-9, a counter, sink or stove 10-12, a bed top 5. (5) Wheels, jars, tyres and anything lying flat use the ground scale. Hand tools stay at hand scale for readability, and an item lying on the ground is drawn at the size it has in the hand. (6) The goal is no stretch factor per family: draw each object at the size the rule gives. Stretching is allowed only as a first step. Heights count from whatever floor someone stands on. Worked values: door 34, shutter opening 45, ground floor 48 (3 m clear, with the sign band above it), upper floor 24 (3 m), parapet 8, car roof 23, van 37, bus 50, army truck 48, 3-storey shophouse 104, 7-storey flats 200, lamp 88, pole 104, street tree 90-103, BTS rail 112.

judge.occlusion_plan:
FACTS: A building hides exactly h px of ground north of its back wall, because the roof is the footprint lifted by h (building_prop.gd:59, 72). A soi is 48 px (city_gen.gd:28), so today's 2- and 3-storey shophouses (58/82) ALREADY hide the whole soi behind them plus 10-34 px of the opposite fronts. Today's only remedy is the fade in main.gd:1296-1339: alpha 0.3 on a building that overlaps the LOCAL player's 12x28 body, trees within dy 0..3 and dx +/-2, and the BTS/skywalk when you are under it. A zombie in your line of sight, in the same soi but under a neighbour's roof, stays hidden today. At zoom 4 (main.gd:131) the 1280x720 view shows 320x180 world px (20 x 11 cells), centred on the chest (main.gd:1040).

PLAN:
(1) Heights grow only where the eye compares them with a person. Each shophouse grows by 22 px (ground floor +18, parapet +4): 3-storey 82 -> 104, which is +1.4 cells of roof. Upper storeys stay at 24. A 3-storey front plus the person still fits comfortably in the 180-px view, so there is no zoom change.
(2) Fix 3 ships first: the see-through trigger becomes 'any character you can currently see' (sight_k > 0.5 on your floor) plus your own body. For each such character, walk up to 7 cells south (world.building_at) and fade a building whose visual_rect meets that character's body rect and whose front is south of its feet. Trees do the same in a dy 0..6, dx -3..3 window. Run at 10 Hz, hold for 0.4 s, tween over 0.16 s. Cost: at most ~60 characters x 7 dictionary lookups, 10 times a second, and no redraw.
(3) An empty soi under a roof stays hidden. That is realistic: from the street you cannot see into a 3 m lane between tall buildings, and the rule never reveals anything outside your line of sight. It is not a dark shade (rejected by the user): only occluders turn see-through, and people keep their existing sight fade.
(4) Inside a building with the roof lifted, fade its front doors, shutters and windows (34-45 px would otherwise cover 2-3 rows of the shop floor). Tall furniture grows only 2-5 px, so no furniture fade is needed now.
(5) Thin things (poles, lamps, pillars, wires) hide nothing. The BTS at 112 follows BTS_H in the existing under-deck fade (main.gd:1320-1339). In Victory the line runs north-south, so lifting it mostly slides it along itself; check the east-west parts of bts_path and bts_row towns.
(6) Tree crowns sit above heads (underside 44-58 px), so people are seen under them, and the wider fade covers the rest.
(7) Compound walls get a 1 m solid base plus a see-through railing, so what is behind them stays readable.
(8) Perf: all art stays static MeshCanvas. Per-frame character drawing is unchanged. Taller visual_rects stream a few more building nodes (world.gd:140); measure on web as per the perf order.
(9) Fallback if a street feels over-ghosted during a horde: cap faded buildings at ~6, nearest to the player first. Last resort (not planned): A's clip-shader peel.
decisions_for_user: Look: after seeing the before/after mock, approve 'true size up to 3 m, half-scale sky' (tall shop floor, squatter upper floors, taller poles, trees and BTS). The alternatives are full true scale with roofs cut away near you, or keeping today's look.

People: keep today's big-head, short-leg character for now (recommended; it is the art style, and it costs about 220 hand-set numbers to change), or plan a reproportion later (head about 1:5 of body height, longer legs, same height). That is the biggest remaining 'toy' cue, and it gets its own mock first.
Upper storeys: keep 24 px, half the 48-px shop floor (recommended: less roof over the street), or 28 px (closer to real; each storey hides about 0.25 cell more ground).
Vehicles: block their longer bodies now with a no-reset pass (recommended; the city stays the same), or wait and do car footprints in the one later city reset.
Trees: pruned street trees 8-10 m with 3.5-4.7 m crowns (recommended), or big spreading rain trees (more shade, far more hidden ground).
City reset (GEN bump) later, in one go: when may we reset cities for 2-cell sofas, family beds and exam couches, full-length stairs, 5-cell sois, real pole spacing and a wider BTS deck?

judge.rejected:
Rejected A (true 16 px/m in every direction, clip-shader roof peel, default zoom 3). FACT: a 3-storey front would be 172 px and a 7-storey block 376 px, while zoom 4 shows 180 px, so every building between the camera and you must be cut to one storey. That is a new shader system, and roofs pop as zombies move: a stage-set cut that is less realistic moment to moment. Zoom 3 would also shrink the hand-built characters on screen. Effort L, the highest risk for a solo beginner, and user taste is unknown. KEPT from A: the diagnosis (roofs are already drawn at 16 px/m depth while walls are at 8 px/m), items on the ground at real size, native redraws instead of stretches as the end state, BTS pillars at ground-scale width, and 'prototype before committing'.

Rejected B's piecewise curve below 2 m (hip-anchored, about 24 px/m between hip and crown). It gives almost the same numbers as C, but a beginner has to evaluate a curve for every object. C's two-slope rule plus the same 'below the hip, match the body' clause is simpler. KEPT from B: the occlusion trigger (fade what covers any character you can see, 10 Hz, hold, tween), the helper World.up(m), and its numbers for rejecting one uniform scale (at 8 px/m the person would be 13 px with 0.27-px eyes; at 11 px/m people would shrink and roofs grow).

Rejected C's 'look box' fade (a 6-cell box around the player). It fades neighbouring roofs even when nothing is under them, so the street looks ghosted all the time. B's seen-character trigger reveals only what matters. Also rejected C's 'leave bikes unchanged': once cars drop to 23 px, bike mirrors (25-31 px) and seated riders (34.5 px) would stand above car roofs.

Also rejected:
- Raising the one VEHICLE_SCALE (2.32 gives the sedan its 4.5 m but a 39-px, 2.5 m roof). The per-kind ratios are wrong in different directions.
- Stretch factors as the final state (they distort line widths; shutter ribs come out 1.3 px thick). They are allowed only as the first step.
- Shrinking the person 2.6 px to exactly 1.65 m (it touches every character file for a 10% gain).
- Silhouettes of hidden characters (a second GDScript draw per character, which is the frame cost).
- Any dark shade over unseen areas (the user already rejected it).
- Changing the camera angle (out of scope).
- Changing VEHICLE_CELLS, SOI_W or plot widths now (they need a GEN bump; batched in fix 12).
